QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_46

question.text: Bhagirathi Growth AIF co-invests in a portfolio company through a joint venture with existing LPs of the fund. Which PPM risk factor is most directly engaged?

answer.text: Co-investments - joint and several liabilities for the investment manager may impact fund performance; contribution-agreement negotiation is critical.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 138-139), the co-investments risk factor states that an AIF may invest in assets through joint ventures or other co-investment structures with existing investors of the fund, that such investments may carry joint and several liabilities for the investment manager and impact fund performance, and that the co-investment arrangement and contribution agreements must be negotiated well with the other co-investors. The Trap: Foreign exchange (B) applies only to offshore-currency exposures. Macroeconomic risk (C) is the broad market/economy risk category. Reputational risk (D) sits with track-record and successor-fund considerations, not co-investment structuring. Note: Page 77 introduces the basic co-investment concept; the PPM risk-factor wording with joint-and-several liabilities and contribution-agreement negotiation comes from pages 138-139.
